extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, essayists, comic writers, and general readers interested in humour, satire, and theatrical decorum
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for producing humour in conversation and on the stage: how laughter arises, how to compose comic 'butts' and characters, when bawdry is a defect, and how playwrights should handle vice and decorum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superiority as source of laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Laughter requires comparing the person we laugh at with an Object below him; persons we laugh at may be wiser than ourselves, but they must 'fall short of us in those Respects which stir up this Passion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the superiority idea when creating targets of ridicule: the comic effect depends on a real or apparent inferiority in some respect. Examples: social inferiority, oddness, infirmity. The passage emphasises that laughter is produced by perceived shortfall, not necessarily general stupidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter from oddness or infirmity in character/representation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a man of wit makes us laugh, it is by betraying some Oddness or Infirmity in his own Character, or in the Representation which he makes of others; when we laugh at a Brute or an inanimate thing, it is at some Action or Incident that bears a remote Analogy to any Blunder or Absurdity in reasonable Creatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humour can be built by exposing an unexpected quirk or failing in a character or by finding human-like blunders in non-human actions. Use analogy and exaggerated infirmity to provoke mirth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for a good 'Butt' in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Man is not qualified for a 'Butt', who has not a good deal of Wit and Vivacity, even in the ridiculous side of his Character; a stupid Butt is only fit for the Conversation of ordinary People.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the conversational target (Butt) to have enough quickness to give play to others; a capable Butt will enliven wit and may even turn ridicule upon his attackers. Anti-pattern: a genuinely stupid target who offers no comedic material except crudeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Butt should give play by active absurdity
rubrics_metrics.description: Men of Wit require one that will give them Play, and bestir himself in the absurd Part of his Behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the Butt participatory: their own active, absurd behavior fuels others' wit. Passive or inert targets reduce opportunities for repartee and comic development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bawdy (luscious expressions) as symptom of lack of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: No one ever writ Bawdy for any other Reason but Dearth of Invention. When the Author cannot strike out of himself any more of that which he has superior to those who make up the Bulk of his Audience, his natural Recourse is to that which he has in common with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat extensive lascivious content as a red flag in evaluating plays/writing: it often substitutes for wit. Use sparingly and only with clear artistic justification; otherwise it signals poverty of imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lascivious gesture and double entendre as devices to enliven weak writing
rubrics_metrics.description: It lifts an heavy empty Sentence, when there is added to it a lascivious Gesture of Body; and when it is too low to be raised even by that, a flat Meaning is enlivened by making it a double one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise these as cheap audience-pleasers used by writers lacking stronger material. They can produce immediate laughs but at the cost of literary/ethical quality and audience respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage exits/exposure and audience complicity are problematic
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Actors make their Exit on this good Occasion, the Ladies are sure to have an examining Glance from the Pit... Such Incidents as these make some Ladies wholly absent themselves from the Play-House; and others never miss the first Day of a Play, lest it should prove too luscious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate stage business that sexualises actors or invites audience voyeurism negatively: it alienates portions of the audience and degrades theatrical dignity. Prefer actions that respect audience sensibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playwrights should use comedy to reform vice, not reward it
rubrics_metrics.description: If Men of Wit... would turn their Thoughts upon raising it from good natural Impulses... they would not only please, but befriend us at the same time... might not such a one divert the Audience quite as well, if at the Catastrophe he were found out for a Traitor, and met with Contempt accordingly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing comic plots, prefer resolutions that expose and punish vice instead of rewarding rakes and deceivers. Use comedy to encourage virtuous behaviour; this both amuses and benefits society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe conversational roles to generate humour
rubrics_metrics.description: When you fall into a Man's Conversation, the first thing you should consider is, whether he has a greater Inclination to hear you, or that you should hear him... there are able Flatterers that never speak a Word in Praise... but practise a skilful Attention to whatever is uttered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft humour from social dynamics: identify who talks vs who listens, who flatters, who imitates. Create characters (e.g., the talkative vanity, the skilful flatterer) whose interactions naturally produce comedic situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic value in social archetypes and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Coffee-house... Men differ rather in the Time of Day in which they make a Figure... The persons to whose Behaviour and Discourse I have most regard, are such as have not Spirits too Active... These are the Men formed for Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recognizable social archetypes (early-morning boasters, fashionable loungers, steady sensible men) and their timing/setting to produce comic contrast. Satire of everyday social roles yields sustained humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Believability requires appropriate costume and props
rubrics_metrics.description: If you cannot prevail to send us the Furniture you forbid at the Play-house, the Heroes appear only like sturdy Beggars, and the Heroines Gipsies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate theatrical production on whether costume/props match character and status; mismatches undermine credibility and humour often becomes unintentional mockery. Anti-pattern: slovenly or anachronistic dress producing ridicule for the wrong reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience imitation amplifies comic influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Eubulus has so great an Authority... that when he shakes his Head at any Piece of publick News, they all of them appear dejected... Nay, their Veneration towards him is so great, that when they are in other Company they speak and act after him; are Wise in his Sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create leading comic voices whose reactions others imitate; the mimicry of characters increases comedic reach and offers material for satire (showing how sway shapes group mood).
